At zero, equal aggregate endpoint weights combine to a point in 3T/4⊂T; after any middle-fiber weight the section remains inside T, and the supplied T provides the reverse inclusion.

Dilation of a triangle by 3/4 multiplies area by 9/16. Exact area is V=1/2 and total area is 17V/8=17/16. The simplex-depth fact is normalized; multiplying by each triangle area gives ordinary maxima (9/16,1,9/16)γ₂V and roots (3/4,1,3/4)√(γ₂V). Independently, the vertex cap at a mark whose corresponding barycentric coordinate is at least 1/3 has area at most 4/9 of the triangle, and Grünbaum gives the matching centroid lower bound.

Normalize each affine majorant by √(γ₂V), writing a+bz. The constraints are a≥1 and a±b≥3/4. Both endpoints cannot be contacts since their average would give a=3/4. The five possible nonempty sets are all realized: (a,b)=(1,0) for {0}, (5/4,±1/2) for the endpoint singletons, and (1,±1/4) for adjacent pairs.

The exact retained bounds are γ₂V=2/9 for the middle singleton, (9/16)γ₂V=1/8 for an endpoint singleton, and (25/32)γ₂V=25/144 for either adjacent pair, whose labels are distinct. The full-source target is (17/16)γ₂V=17/72, above 2/9 by 1/72. Verified all numbers independently with rational arithmetic.
